classification.difficultyReason: Identify the relevant right triangles within composite figures and calculate their hypotenuses.

content.prompt: Find the values of $x$ and $y$ in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Two right triangles share a vertical altitude, with the short base segment on the left and the longer segment on the right. Ordinary source-blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Altitude 24 cm; left base 7 cm; right base 45 cm; left hypotenuse x cm; right hypotenuse y cm. The altitude is perpendicular to the base.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem in the left triangle:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=7^2+24^2\\x^2&=49+576\\x^2&=625\\x&=25\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
In the right triangle:
$$\begin{align*}y^2&=24^2+45^2\\y^2&=576+2025\\y^2&=2601\\y&=51\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A lower rectangle and upper right triangle share a red dashed horizontal construction. Retains all three right-angle squares and the redundant 7 cm measurement. Ordinary outlines and labels are black.
spec.mathematics: Bottom width 8 cm; right vertical side 7 cm; upper left vertical segment 8 cm; upper sloping side x cm. The horizontal construction has the same width as the rectangle.
spec.answerVisibility: The construction is supplied, but its inferred length and the calculated hypotenuse are not printed.

answer.worked:
The dashed horizontal segment is $8\text{ cm}$ because it is opposite the bottom side of the rectangle. By Pythagoras’ theorem in the upper triangle:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=8^2+8^2\\x^2&=64+64\\x^2&=128\\x&=\sqrt{128}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
